ADMISSION DIAGNOSIS:
Elena Ellison, a 52-year-old woman, was admitted with acute gallstone pancreatitis. The episode began with persistent upper abdominal discomfort, nausea, and inability to tolerate her usual meals. The treating team attributed the pancreatitis to gallstone disease after reviewing her history and the information available during the admission. There was no reported alcohol use or other clear precipitating event. Her known conditions include hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypothyroidism. These chronic conditions were included in the inpatient care plan. The initial goals were relief of pain and nausea, support of oral hydration and nutrition as tolerated, and close observation for complications. General surgery and gastroenterology participated in planning care. Elena remained in the hospital until her symptoms improved, oral intake resumed, and a definitive plan for gallstone management was completed.
Elena Ellison | MRN-55656 | Discharge summary | Page 2 of 20

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS:
Before arrival, Elena developed abdominal pain that became persistent and was accompanied by nausea and reduced intake. She described the discomfort as interfering with rest and normal activity. She did not report a similar prolonged episode requiring hospital care. The history was consistent with acute pancreatitis related to gallstones. The team reviewed possible contributing factors and did not identify another likely cause from the history obtained. She came to the hospital because symptoms continued despite attempts to rest and take fluids at home. On admission, care focused on symptom relief, bowel rest followed by gradual intake as tolerated, and observation for a worsening course. She and her family received updates about the suspected cause, expected recovery, and the possibility of surgical treatment during this stay. Her symptoms began to ease with supportive inpatient care.
Elena Ellison | MRN-55656 | Discharge summary | Page 3 of 20

RELEVANT MEDICAL HISTORY:
Elena has hypertension, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypothyroidism. These conditions were considered throughout the admission, particularly as her oral intake changed and she prepared for a procedure. She reported no prior episode of gallstone pancreatitis requiring admission. Her history was reviewed with her to identify prior abdominal procedures, allergies, and relevant family or social factors. No additional chronic condition altered the overall treatment plan. Her usual outpatient care had been directed toward ongoing management of her chronic illnesses. During this stay, the team aimed to avoid interruption of necessary chronic care while adapting it to a temporary period of reduced intake and procedural preparation. Elena understood that the admission was primarily for the acute pancreatic illness and that long-term care of her chronic conditions would continue after discharge through her usual outpatient clinicians.
Elena Ellison | MRN-55656 | Discharge summary | Page 4 of 20

INITIAL INPATIENT ASSESSMENT:
The admitting team assessed Elena’s symptoms as acute pancreatitis associated with gallstones. The immediate approach was supportive care, including relief of discomfort and nausea, fluid support, and temporary limitation of food while symptoms were active. The team planned to advance her diet when she could tolerate it. She was observed for persistent pain, inability to resume intake, or other signs of a complicated course. The cause and treatment options were discussed in plain language, including the role of gallbladder removal in preventing another episode. Her hypertension, diabetes, and hypothyroidism were accounted for in the care plan. Gastroenterology and general surgery were asked to contribute recommendations. Elena was able to participate in decisions and expressed agreement with the proposed approach. The early plan emphasized recovery from inflammation before proceeding with definitive gallstone treatment.
Elena Ellison | MRN-55656 | Discharge summary | Page 5 of 20

FIRST HOSPITAL DAY:
During the first hospital day, Elena received supportive care for acute pancreatitis. Her abdominal discomfort and nausea remained the main concerns, and oral intake was limited while symptoms were prominent. The inpatient team adjusted the care plan according to her reported comfort and ability to drink. Staff encouraged rest and explained that food would be reintroduced gradually as she improved. Her care team reviewed the suspected gallstone cause and discussed that removal of the gallbladder could reduce the risk of recurrence. General surgery and gastroenterology reviewed the case and coordinated their recommendations with the admitting service. No separate urgent intervention was required at that point. Elena remained engaged in discussions and asked appropriate questions about recovery and the anticipated length of stay. Her chronic conditions continued to be considered while the acute illness was managed.
Elena Ellison | MRN-55656 | Discharge summary | Page 6 of 20

SECOND HOSPITAL DAY:
On the second hospital day, Elena reported that the abdominal discomfort was easing, although she was not yet ready for a full diet. Nausea also became less troublesome with supportive care. The team continued to encourage oral fluids and planned a gradual diet advance based on her tolerance. General surgery reviewed the timing and expected benefits of gallbladder removal during this admission. Gastroenterology agreed that a procedure to clear the bile duct was not indicated based on the clinical course available to the team. The plan remained to allow the acute inflammation to settle and then proceed with definitive gallstone treatment if improvement continued. Elena was updated about the sequence of care and the usual recovery period. Her diabetes and other chronic conditions remained part of routine inpatient planning.
Elena Ellison | MRN-55656 | Discharge summary | Page 7 of 20

THIRD HOSPITAL DAY:
By the third hospital day, Elena described continued improvement and was able to take small amounts by mouth without a return of severe nausea. Her pain was manageable, and she was more comfortable discussing the next step in treatment. The team advanced her diet as tolerated and monitored for recurrence of symptoms. General surgery evaluated her readiness for laparoscopic gallbladder removal. The procedure was planned during the admission to address the source of the pancreatitis and reduce the chance of another attack. The team reviewed expected benefits, common risks, and postoperative expectations with Elena. She agreed to proceed. Her family was kept informed at her request. No new concern changed the overall plan, and she continued to make steady progress with supportive care.
Elena Ellison | MRN-55656 | Discharge summary | Page 8 of 20

FOURTH HOSPITAL DAY:
On the fourth hospital day, Elena continued to improve and proceeded with laparoscopic removal of the gallbladder. She had been informed about the purpose of the procedure and the expected short-term recovery. The operation was completed without a reported complication. Afterward, she rested and resumed oral intake gradually as tolerated. The care team reviewed postoperative comfort measures and encouraged movement when she felt ready. Her abdominal symptoms remained improved compared with admission. She and her family were told that mild soreness around the incision area could occur during recovery and should lessen over time. The team continued to assess whether she could manage meals, walking, and routine self-care before discharge. Her recovery remained on the expected course, and no additional inpatient procedure was planned.
Elena Ellison | MRN-55656 | Discharge summary | Page 9 of 20

FIFTH HOSPITAL DAY:
During the fifth hospital day, Elena continued recovery after gallbladder removal. She tolerated progressively more food and fluids and did not report a return of the severe pain or nausea that brought her to the hospital. She was able to get out of bed and walk with minimal assistance. The surgical team reviewed wound care and activity guidance, while the admitting team confirmed that her pancreatic symptoms had settled sufficiently for discharge planning. Her chronic conditions were reviewed with attention to resuming her usual outpatient routine through her established care. The team discussed warning symptoms that would require prompt medical attention. Elena felt ready to continue recovery at home, and her family confirmed that support would be available. Discharge was planned once the remaining routine arrangements were completed.
Elena Ellison | MRN-55656 | Discharge summary | Page 10 of 20

GASTROENTEROLOGY INPUT:
Gastroenterology reviewed Elena’s presentation and agreed with the diagnosis of gallstone pancreatitis. The service recommended supportive care and observation for improvement, with attention to pain, nausea, hydration, and return of oral intake. The team did not recommend a bile duct procedure during this admission because the clinical course did not suggest a need for one. Gastroenterology supported definitive gallbladder treatment once Elena had improved enough to proceed safely. Their recommendations were discussed with general surgery and the admitting team so that care remained coordinated. Elena received an explanation that treatment of the gallbladder source was intended to lower the chance of another pancreatitis episode. No separate outpatient gastroenterology appointment was considered necessary unless symptoms returned or her usual clinicians identified a new concern. She was encouraged to seek care promptly for recurrent severe abdominal pain, persistent vomiting, or inability to drink.
Elena Ellison | MRN-55656 | Discharge summary | Page 11 of 20

GENERAL SURGERY INPUT:
General surgery reviewed Elena’s gallstone pancreatitis and recommended removal of the gallbladder during this admission after her acute symptoms improved. The surgeon discussed the reason for the procedure, the expected benefits, alternatives, and potential complications with Elena. She was given an opportunity to ask questions and agreed with the plan. The surgical team coordinated timing with the admitting service and gastroenterology. Laparoscopic removal was completed without a reported complication. After the procedure, the surgical team reviewed incision care, gradual return to usual activity, and the need to avoid strenuous exertion until recovery progressed. They also reviewed symptoms that should prompt urgent evaluation, including worsening abdominal pain, fever, persistent vomiting, or problems at an incision. Routine surgical follow-up was arranged to assess healing and review any concerns. No additional operative treatment was planned before discharge.
Elena Ellison | MRN-55656 | Discharge summary | Page 12 of 20

PROCEDURES:
Elena underwent laparoscopic cholecystectomy during the admission for gallstone pancreatitis. The procedure addressed the suspected source of the acute illness and was selected after her symptoms improved enough for surgery. The operative course was reported as uncomplicated. No other procedure was required during this stay. Following surgery, Elena was observed as she recovered from the effects of the procedure and gradually resumed oral intake. The surgical team provided instructions about keeping the incision areas clean and dry and avoiding strenuous activity during early healing. She was advised to contact the surgical service if she noticed increasing redness, drainage, opening of an incision, or worsening pain. The operation was explained to her as a preventive step intended to reduce the risk of recurrent gallstone-related illness. She understood the reason for treatment and agreed with the recovery plan.
Elena Ellison | MRN-55656 | Discharge summary | Page 13 of 20

TREATMENT DURING ADMISSION:
